findings.title: Approved end-user browser workflow is still absent, so AC-009 is unsatisfied in the product surface users are supposed to ship
evidence: AC `LLMRD-AC-009` explicitly requires a dedicated browser-visible workflow for route creation, release registration, deploy initiation, approval visibility, and route-state/activity observation.
`verification_report.md` marks `LLMRD-AC-009` as `Failed` and records that no dedicated LLM workflow exists under `web/src/routes`.
`test_matrix.json` shows `LLMRD-T-018` blocked because no dedicated end-user LLM workflow exists.
`defects.json` records `LLMRD-D-001` as an open major defect, and `hitl_decisions.md` decision `HITL-LLM_ROUTE_RELEASE_DEPLOYMENT-008` classifies it as a `BLOCKER`.
findings.suggested_action: Do not treat the current shared-store visibility plus REST-compatibility evidence as release-worthy substitute behavior. Implement the dedicated browser workflow and unblock the corresponding E2E proof.

findings.title: Several accepted deployment failure branches can fail the run without emitting the terminal error reply AC-006 requires
evidence: `internal/service/llm_provisioning_coordinator.go:108-127` calls `failRun(...)` before `req` is populated when loading the intent fails, the intent is missing, route/release/environment loading fails, candidate selection fails, or provisioner resolution fails.
`internal/service/llm_provisioning_coordinator.go:220-236` only calls `publishError(...)` when `req.Route`, `req.Release`, and `req.Environment` are all non-nil.
That means early post-acceptance failures can mark the run failed via `registry.CompleteDeploymentRun(..., domain.RunStatusFailed, ...)` but emit no terminal responder error event at all.

AC `LLMRD-AC-006` requires that accepted deployments eventually publish a terminal `7973` error result for failures, and `test_matrix.json` shows the success/failure coordinator tests (`LLMRD-T-012`, `LLMRD-T-013`) are still not implemented.
findings.suggested_action: Patch the coordinator failure path so every accepted deployment failure emits a terminal error result with enough correlation data, then add focused success/failure coordinator tests to prove it.

findings.title: Route creation and release registration still bypass the canonical signer-first request path, so AC-002 and AC-003 are weaker than the accepted product contract suggests
evidence: `internal/controlplane/llm_command_publisher.go` only implements `PublishLLMDeployRequest`, `PublishLLMApprovalRequest`, and `PublishLLMRollbackRequest`; there is no publisher method for route-create (`5971`) or release-register (`5972`).
`internal/mcp/server.go:77-82` defines the MCP `LLMCommandPublisher` interface with only deploy, approval, and rollback methods.

`internal/mcp/server.go:2341-2460` shows `handleLLMCreateRoute` and `handleLLMRegisterRelease` directly calling `registry.CreateRoute(...)` and `registry.CreateRelease(...)` instead of publishing canonical signed Nostr requests.
`verification_report.md` already marks `LLMRD-AC-002` and `LLMRD-AC-003` only partially verified, and `defects.json` records `LLMRD-D-005` as an open gap.

`hitl_decisions.md` accepts `D-005` as release risk, but the source evidence shows this is not only a missing test; the current requester-facing MCP path is structurally different from the accepted signer-first contract.
findings.suggested_action: Either implement canonical requester-side 5971/5972 publishing for route/release operations and test relay-acceptance behavior, or narrow the accepted contract so direct registry mutation is explicitly allowed for this release. The current state mixes both stories.

proposed_hitl_question.question: How should route creation and release registration be treated for this release given that current MCP tooling still mutates the registry directly instead of publishing canonical 5971/5972 requests?
options: Require canonical signer-first 5971/5972 request publishing before release
Allow direct MCP registry mutation as a temporary compatibility path for this release
Defer route/release creation from the approved release scope until canonical publishing exists
Revise AC-002 and AC-003 to describe the mixed contract explicitly

findings.title: Schema-backed artifact validation is missing, which weakens machine-checkable review discipline
evidence: The requested schema file `schemas/adversarial_review.schema.json` was not present in the repository.
The earlier confidence step also recorded that `schemas/confidence_report.schema.json` was missing.
Without the schema files, artifact structure cannot be validated mechanically even though the prompts require schema conformance.
findings.suggested_action: Add the missing schema files or document the canonical JSON structure in-repo so future PSTF artifacts can be validated automatically.
